tools.name: dv360_native_action
tools.description: Execute any Display & Video 360 v4 REST action from the generated docs-backed catalog. Use canonical DV360_* actions such as DV360_ADVERTISERS_LIST, or resource + method such as resource=advertisers and method=list. Pass path/query parameters through params, pathParams, or query; pass create/update request bodies through body or payload. body/payload may also be nested under params and may be a JSON object or a stringified JSON object. Campaign flow: create the paused campaign shell with create_campaign or DV360_ADVERTISERS_CAMPAIGNS_CREATE, create the insertion order with DV360_ADVERTISERS_INSERTION_ORDERS_CREATE, create display/video/audio/Demand Gen or explicit YouTube & Partners line items with create_adset or DV360_ADVERTISERS_LINE_ITEMS_CREATE, then upload/create/assign creatives before activating. For YouTube & Partners line item writes, provide the exact lineItemType and bidStrategy.youtubeAndPartnersBid. Existing DV360 accounts can return YouTube & Partners line items through read/list, so MCP does not locally block explicit payloads; Google remains the final authority for account/type-specific write support. For creative assets use DV360_ADVERTISERS_ASSETS_UPLOAD with advertiserId plus body/payload { filename, mediaBase64 or mediaContent, mimeType }. For generic media upload use DV360_MEDIA_UPLOAD with resourceName plus mediaBase64 or mediaContent and mimeType; the backend adds upload_type=media. For generic media download use DV360_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD with resourceName; the backend adds alt=media. For creative creation use DV360_ADVERTISERS_CREATIVES_CREATE or the semantic create_creative tool, then assign creatives by patching DV360_ADVERTISERS_LINE_ITEMS_PATCH with updateMask=creativeIds. For YouTube line item asset launch work, manage location lists with DV360_ADVERTISERS_LOCATION_LISTS_* and link sitelink/location assets with DV360_ADVERTISERS_LINE_ITEMS_YOUTUBE_ASSET_TYPES_YOUTUBE_ASSET_ASSOCIATIONS_*; Google marks association create/delete as available only to an informed subset of users. For location/POI/business-chain lookup, use DV360_TARGETING_TYPES_TARGETING_OPTIONS_SEARCH with targetingType plus advertiserId and body aliases such as searchTerms/query; MCP normalizes them to geoRegionSearchTerms.geoRegionQuery, poiSearchTerms.poiQuery, or businessChainSearchTerms.businessChainQuery. Do not guess geo targetingOptionId values. For interests/audiences such as cars, do not use targetingOptions.search. Use DV360_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES_LIST, DV360_CUSTOM_LISTS_LIST, DV360_COMBINED_AUDIENCES_LIST, and/or DV360_FIRST_PARTY_AND_PARTNER_AUDIENCES_LIST with advertiserId or partnerId and query/searchTerms/displayName; MCP normalizes those aliases to the documented displayName filter. Target selected results with TARGETING_TYPE_AUDIENCE_GROUP via audienceGroupDetails. For channels and inventory/deal discovery, use DV360_ADVERTISERS_CHANNELS_LIST, DV360_PARTNERS_CHANNELS_LIST, DV360_INVENTORY_SOURCES_LIST, or DV360_INVENTORY_SOURCE_GROUPS_LIST with query/searchTerms/displayName; MCP normalizes supported displayName filters. For finite targeting taxonomies such as categories, devices, browsers, languages, and exchanges, use DV360_TARGETING_TYPES_TARGETING_OPTIONS_LIST and filter returned names client-side unless the docs expose a server filter. For Bid Manager reports, standard report runs, query runs, report retrieval, or report listing, use dv360_reporting_ops instead of this generic REST tool. Write actions default to dry_run: true and require confirmed: true when dry_run is false.

operations.description:
Create a new ad campaign on any supported platform. SAFETY: dry_run defaults to true — always preview the payload before executing. Campaigns are ALWAYS created in PAUSED status regardless of input. Use publish_campaign to activate. Before calling create_campaign, first run plan_campaign_structure for supported generic platforms so the MCP inspects workspace assets, recent campaign patterns, and likely structure. Set idempotency_key (UUID) to prevent duplicate creation on retries. You can pass source_campaign_id plus autofill_from_history=true to reuse safe defaults from a historical campaign snapshot. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok campaign launch is native-only on MCP; use meta_*, snapchat_*, and tiktok_* native create/update/report tools. 

Objective values by platform:
  X: REACH, ENGAGEMENTS, WEBSITE_CLICKS, VIDEO_VIEWS, APP_INSTALLS, WEBSITE_CONVERSIONS, APP_ENGAGEMENTS, FOLLOWERS, PREROLL_VIEWS. X app line-item goals include APP_CLICKS, APP_INSTALLS, and APP_PURCHASES.
  DV360: AWARENESS, TRAFFIC, SALES, LEADS, APP_INSTALLS, VIDEO, DEMAND_GEN

Budget units: USD for DV360 campaign planned spend only; serving budget is set on insertion orders and line items.
DV360 note: create_campaign creates the paused campaign shell only. Create insertion orders with dv360_native_action DV360_ADVERTISERS_INSERTION_ORDERS_CREATE, line items with create_adset or DV360_ADVERTISERS_LINE_ITEMS_CREATE, then upload/create/assign creatives before activation.
Requires scope: write:campaigns.

operations.description: Transfer a campaign from one advertising platform to another using the same AMCP cross-transfer workflow as the main system. The backend fetches the full source tree (campaign, ad sets, ads), maps entities to the destination platform, migrates media first, then creates destination campaign/ad sets/ads in the requested safe execution mode. Supports Builder-equivalent partial transfers (campaign-only, selected ad sets, selected ads), multi-asset expansion, and destination-side field overrides such as objective or budget before publish. Production-safe flow: dry_run defaults to true for preview; when dry_run is false the backend rebuilds the current migration plan inline and executes only if the plan is ready. Meta to Snapchat/TikTok guardrail: only story-compatible vertical assets are uploaded; ads without a compatible vertical asset are flagged and skipped instead of forcing a bad 1:1 or landscape creative. SAFETY: dry_run defaults to true. dry_run=false with execution_mode=create_paused creates destination entities paused; no separate migration_plan_id or confirmed flag is required. Supported production platforms are Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, and Google. Google is supported as a transfer target (Search/Display/Video/Demand Gen via the standard tree; Performance Max via the asset-group orchestrator). Do not use this tool for DV360, Adjust, LinkedIn, X, Reddit, or OpenAI Ads until a platform-specific mapper exists. Use destination_credentials when the destination platform needs page/profile/identity context for ad creation, such as Meta Page, Snapchat Public Profile, or TikTok Identity. Requires scope: write:campaigns.

operations.description: Generate AI-powered ad copy including headlines, descriptions, primary text, and CTAs. Supports tone control (professional, casual, urgent, playful) and platform-specific optimization. IMPORTANT: Always review generated content before applying to campaigns. AI-generated content is a starting point — it should be human-reviewed and edited. Rate limited: 5 requests per minute. Requires scope: read:campaigns.

operations.description: Generate AI image creatives from an existing ad, preview context, product catalog context, or a plain prompt. The generated assets are saved to the AMCP media library and can optionally be uploaded to a connected platform account. This consumes AI/image generation credits and writes workspace assets, so it requires write:campaigns. Always review generated assets before launching campaigns.

operations.description: Preview how an ad will look before publishing. Supports LinkedIn accurate/live ad previews, Reddit ad/post preview links, and OpenAI chat-card payload preview fallback. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok previews are native-only. Returns the richest preview URL or iframe/html payload the backend can resolve. Preview URLs may expire — re-fetch if the link stops working. Requires scope: read:campaigns.

For large accounts, prefer fetch_campaign -> fetch_adsets -> fetch_ads -> fetch_creatives to avoid backend timeouts. For Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok, use native read tools. Returns campaign settings, targeting, ad creatives, and performance metrics. Use this before update_entities to understand current settings. Requires scope: read:campaigns.

Uses the platform-native full creative, media preview, thumbnail, image/video lookup, and Smart Creative actions that the main system already relies on for reporting and transfer workflows. Use this before cloning/adapting an existing ad on supported generic platforms. For Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok, use native creative/media tools. Useful when you need raw creative payloads, ordered carousel cards, resolved download/preview URLs, thumbnails, or ACO materials inside MCP.

operations.description: Get data-driven optimization recommendations for a campaign. Analyzes performance trends to suggest budget reallocations, bid adjustments, creative refreshes, and targeting improvements. Runs audit_campaign internally, then generates AI-powered recommendations from the findings. Returns prioritized suggestions with rationale and specific action steps. Requires scope: read:reports.

operations.description: Fetch performance metrics for campaigns on a platform. Returns impressions, clicks, spend, CPM, CTR, CPC, conversions, and ROAS. Supports daily, monthly, or total granularity. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok reporting is native-only on MCP; use this generic report tool for the remaining generic platforms. Can compare campaigns, attach historical context, and explain why one campaign performed better than another using real backend rows only. Data is always fresh — not cached. Requires scope: read:reports.

operations.description: Get the Google Ads search terms report — real search queries that triggered your ads. Shows which search terms are driving impressions, clicks, and conversions. operations.description: Inspect the account, workspace assets, and recent campaign structure before creating anything. Returns a strategy recommendation for how many ad sets/ad groups and ads to launch, plus the likely missing or ambiguous assets. Use this before create_campaign and create_adset so the build flow matches the business model, account history, and platform constraints. This is a planning/preflight tool: it does not create anything and it does not replace verified taxonomy lookups. Requires scopes: read:accounts and read:campaigns.

operations.description: Unified upload parity tool for both the legacy direct platform upload routes and the system-backed creative-assets upload flow. Use UPLOAD_LOCAL_FILE or UPLOAD_FROM_URL_VIA_SESSION when you want the same storage + Inngest + creative_assets lineage used by the main app. GET_SIGNED_URL / CONFIRM_UPLOAD and direct UPLOAD_FROM_URL remain available for low-level parity workflows. Storage-backed upload sessions support Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, google, openai, x (Twitter Ads), reddit, linkedin, DV360, and Criteo targets. Direct UPLOAD_FROM_URL uses the platform upload adapter where available. Google images are registered through Google Ads AssetService and return uploaded_asset / google_asset_resource_name; Google videos require a YouTube URL or 11-character video ID and return a YouTube video asset. DV360 uploads use dv360_native_action because they require advertiser-scoped DV360 asset/adAsset endpoints. For X, the call returns x_media_key — bind it to a tweet via x_creative_ops CREATE_TWEET (with media_keys) before promoting. After upload/import completes, call list_media_assets to pick up the final platform-specific IDs used by create payloads. dry_run defaults to true for mutating upload flows.

operations.description:
Update a campaign, ad set, or ad on any platform. SAFETY: dry_run defaults to true — always preview the diff before executing. Immutable fields are automatically blocked with workaround instructions. Read the field-rules resource before calling to know which fields are editable. When an upstream validation error mentions a missing parent context or unsupported field combination, re-check platform-capabilities and the platform’s official docs before retrying; do not blindly repeat the same payload. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok updates are native-only on MCP; use their native update/status tools. 

Common editable fields:
  Campaign: name, status, daily_budget, lifetime_budget, bid_strategy
  Ad Set: name, status, targeting, bid_amount, daily_budget, end_time
  Ad: name, status, creative

Status values: Google uses ENABLED/PAUSED. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok status updates are native-only.
Requires scope: write:campaigns.

tools.description: Google Analytics 4 gateway for OAuth, properties, metadata, reports, async report tasks, and audience exports.

arguments.description: Exact arguments for the selected operation. The original operation schema is validated before execution.

operations.description: Read/query/list GA4 audience exports. Query results may contain user-level audience data; summarize before showing to the LLM/user. Requires scope: read:reports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

audience_export_name.description: Full audience export resource name, e.g. properties/{id}/audienceExports/{export_id}.

request.description: Query request body or audienceExportId fallback.

operations.description: Start, complete, refresh, inspect, or disconnect the Google Analytics 4 OAuth connection. Uses analytics.readonly and encrypted token storage. Mutating actions require dry_run=false after approval. Requires read:reports for status and write:exports for connection changes.

state.description: Signed OAuth state returned by start.

redirect_uri.description: OAuth redirect URI. Defaults to GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_REDIRECT_URI or /auth/google-analytics.

connection_id.description: Optional GA4 connection ID.

dry_run.description: Preview mutating operations without storing/revoking tokens.

operations.description: Create a GA4 audience export. This can expose user-level audience membership snapshots, so use only when explicitly requested. Requires scope: write:exports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

request.description: Native Google Analytics Data API request body.

dry_run.description: Preview the audience export creation without creating a Google export.

operations.description: Create an async GA4 report task for large report jobs. The task is retained by Google for a limited time and tracked in AMCP. Requires scope: write:exports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

request.description: Native Google Analytics Data API request body.

dry_run.description: Preview the report task creation without creating a Google async task.

operations.description: Run GA4 Data API batch, realtime, pivot, funnel, or quota snapshot report methods. Requires scope: read:reports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

request.description: Native Google Analytics Data API request body.

operations.description: List stored Google Analytics 4 properties for the workspace. Use ga4_sync_properties first if no properties are stored yet. Requires scope: read:reports.

connection_id.description: Optional GA4 connection ID.

operations.description: Read GA4 Data API metadata or check dimension/metric compatibility before running a report. Requires scope: read:reports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

operations.description: Read/query/list GA4 async report tasks. Requires scope: read:reports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

report_task_name.description: Full report task resource name, e.g. properties/{id}/reportTasks/{task_id}.

request.description: Query request body or reportTaskId fallback.

operations.description: Run a GA4 Data API runReport request. Supports cache, fresh reads, and safe pagination across all rows. For large exports use paginate_all with max_rows, or ga4_create_report_task for async reports. Requires scope: read:reports.

property.description: GA4 property ID, either numeric or properties/{property_id}.

request.description: Native Google Analytics Data API request body.

paginate_all.description: Page through all available rows using the Data API offset/limit controls.

max_rows.description: Maximum rows to return when paginate_all=true.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Cache TTL. Use 0 for no cache.

operations.description: Discover accessible Google Analytics accounts/properties through the Analytics Admin API and persist them for the workspace. This does not change Google Analytics; it updates AMCP connection metadata. Requires scope: write:exports.

connection_id.description: Optional GA4 connection ID.

include_details.description: Fetch per-property details such as currency and timezone.

max_pages.description: Maximum Admin API account summary pages to scan.

dry_run.description: Preview the sync without storing property metadata.

Raw API payload mode is the default; set payload_mode="form" explicitly to use the shared compiler/system form path. DV360 create_adset maps to lineItems.create, so parent_id must be the insertionOrderId. Create insertion orders first with dv360_native_action DV360_ADVERTISERS_INSERTION_ORDERS_CREATE. dry_run defaults to true and returns the exact backend request preview.

raw.description:
Create a new ad campaign on any supported platform. SAFETY: dry_run defaults to true — always preview the payload before executing. Campaigns are ALWAYS created in PAUSED status regardless of input. Use publish_campaign to activate. Before calling create_campaign, first run plan_campaign_structure for supported generic platforms so the MCP inspects workspace assets, recent campaign patterns, and likely structure. Set idempotency_key (UUID) to prevent duplicate creation on retries. You can pass source_campaign_id plus autofill_from_history=true to reuse safe defaults from a historical campaign snapshot. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok campaign launch is native-only on MCP; use meta_*, snapchat_*, and tiktok_* native create/update/report tools. 

Objective values by platform:
  X: REACH, ENGAGEMENTS, WEBSITE_CLICKS, VIDEO_VIEWS, APP_INSTALLS, WEBSITE_CONVERSIONS, APP_ENGAGEMENTS, FOLLOWERS, PREROLL_VIEWS. X app line-item goals include APP_CLICKS, APP_INSTALLS, and APP_PURCHASES.
  DV360: AWARENESS, TRAFFIC, SALES, LEADS, APP_INSTALLS, VIDEO, DEMAND_GEN

Budget units: USD for DV360 campaign planned spend only; serving budget is set on insertion orders and line items.
DV360 note: create_campaign creates the paused campaign shell only. Create insertion orders with dv360_native_action DV360_ADVERTISERS_INSERTION_ORDERS_CREATE, line items with create_adset or DV360_ADVERTISERS_LINE_ITEMS_CREATE, then upload/create/assign creatives before activation.
Requires scope: write:campaigns.

raw.description: Transfer a campaign from one advertising platform to another using the same AMCP cross-transfer workflow as the main system. The backend fetches the full source tree (campaign, ad sets, ads), maps entities to the destination platform, migrates media first, then creates destination campaign/ad sets/ads in the requested safe execution mode. Supports Builder-equivalent partial transfers (campaign-only, selected ad sets, selected ads), multi-asset expansion, and destination-side field overrides such as objective or budget before publish. Production-safe flow: dry_run defaults to true for preview; when dry_run is false the backend rebuilds the current migration plan inline and executes only if the plan is ready. Meta to Snapchat/TikTok guardrail: only story-compatible vertical assets are uploaded; ads without a compatible vertical asset are flagged and skipped instead of forcing a bad 1:1 or landscape creative. SAFETY: dry_run defaults to true. dry_run=false with execution_mode=create_paused creates destination entities paused; no separate migration_plan_id or confirmed flag is required. Supported production platforms are Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, and Google. Google is supported as a transfer target (Search/Display/Video/Demand Gen via the standard tree; Performance Max via the asset-group orchestrator). Do not use this tool for DV360, Adjust, LinkedIn, X, Reddit, or OpenAI Ads until a platform-specific mapper exists. Use destination_credentials when the destination platform needs page/profile/identity context for ad creation, such as Meta Page, Snapchat Public Profile, or TikTok Identity. Requires scope: write:campaigns.

raw.description: Unified upload parity tool for both the legacy direct platform upload routes and the system-backed creative-assets upload flow. Use UPLOAD_LOCAL_FILE or UPLOAD_FROM_URL_VIA_SESSION when you want the same storage + Inngest + creative_assets lineage used by the main app. GET_SIGNED_URL / CONFIRM_UPLOAD and direct UPLOAD_FROM_URL remain available for low-level parity workflows. Storage-backed upload sessions support Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, google, openai, x (Twitter Ads), reddit, linkedin, DV360, and Criteo targets. Direct UPLOAD_FROM_URL uses the platform upload adapter where available. Google images are registered through Google Ads AssetService and return uploaded_asset / google_asset_resource_name; Google videos require a YouTube URL or 11-character video ID and return a YouTube video asset. DV360 uploads use dv360_native_action because they require advertiser-scoped DV360 asset/adAsset endpoints. For X, the call returns x_media_key — bind it to a tweet via x_creative_ops CREATE_TWEET (with media_keys) before promoting. After upload/import completes, call list_media_assets to pick up the final platform-specific IDs used by create payloads. dry_run defaults to true for mutating upload flows.

raw.description:
Update a campaign, ad set, or ad on any platform. SAFETY: dry_run defaults to true — always preview the diff before executing. Immutable fields are automatically blocked with workaround instructions. Read the field-rules resource before calling to know which fields are editable. When an upstream validation error mentions a missing parent context or unsupported field combination, re-check platform-capabilities and the platform’s official docs before retrying; do not blindly repeat the same payload. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok updates are native-only on MCP; use their native update/status tools. 

Common editable fields:
  Campaign: name, status, daily_budget, lifetime_budget, bid_strategy
  Ad Set: name, status, targeting, bid_amount, daily_budget, end_time
  Ad: name, status, creative

Status values: Google uses ENABLED/PAUSED. Meta, Snapchat, and TikTok status updates are native-only.
Requires scope: write:campaigns.

Use "form" on Reddit, OpenAI, Google, X, or LinkedIn to merge the requested form changes with the current entity and compile the final update payload through the shared platform compiler. When omitted, raw API mode is used. Set payload_mode="form" explicitly when you want compiler-backed merge/update behavior.

compiler_context.description: Optional extra form context used when payload_mode="form"

dry_run.description: Return a request preview without updating the saved query

raw.description: Update an existing scheduled reporting job.

template_id.description: Optional template ID

timezone.description: Updated timezone

dry_run.description: Return a request preview without updating the schedule

raw.description: Fetch a lightweight AMCP user/workspace context: user, company, billing summary, connected platform summary, and recommended defaults. Use this first to infer workspace defaults. Keep it lightweight by default; call list_accounts or list_workspace_assets only when exact account or asset IDs are needed.

include_accounts.description: Also return discovered ad accounts from list_accounts. Leave false for a fast bootstrap; call list_accounts when you need exhaustive account discovery.

account_limit.description: Maximum accounts returned per platform when include_accounts is true. account_summary still reports total/truncated counts.

include_asset_summary.description: Also return grouped asset counts (pages, profiles, pixels, apps, catalogs, custom conversions) across connected platforms.

include_integration_details.description: Return raw connection and selected asset arrays inside integrations. This can be large; prefer list_workspace_assets for asset details.

raw.description: List all connected ad accounts across Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, Reddit, LinkedIn, Google, OpenAI, X, DV360, and Criteo Retail Media. Returns account IDs, names, currency, and timezone. Use this first to discover which accounts are available before calling other tools. If a platform fails, other platforms still return results (graceful degradation). Requires scope: read:accounts.

platform.description: Filter to a specific connected-account discovery platform (reddit, linkedin, google, openai, x, dv360, criteo, plus meta, snapchat, and tiktok). Cross-platform account discovery includes native-only ad platforms for workspace bootstrap; use native account tools for platform-specific account operations.

include_inactive.description: Include inactive or paused ad accounts. Default: false (active only).

raw.description: List workspace-selected assets across connected platforms in a normalized shape. Use this when you need pages, profiles, pixels, apps, catalogs, custom conversions, or advertiser/ad-account IDs before building payloads. The response preserves each asset's payload_value so the selected row can be reused directly in campaign/ad set/ad payloads.

platform.description: Optional workspace-asset platform filter, including meta, snapchat, and tiktok. Campaign/report/launch operations for those platforms are native-only.

include_items.description: Include grouped asset rows. Disable to fetch counts/coverage only.

include_disconnected.description: Also return disconnected assets. Default: false.

gaps: LIST_ACTIONS unsupported; full action denominator unknown.

raw.description: List connected WooCommerce stores in this AMCP workspace. Use this first to discover store labels before pulling products, orders, or sales reports. Requires scope: read:accounts.

include_disconnected.description: Include stores that were disconnected. Default: false.

raw.description: WooCommerce read-only commerce operations: products, orders, customers, coupons, sales reports, top sellers, Analytics reports/stats, report totals, and custom sales breakdowns by date, product, category, coupon, customer, country, status, or payment method. Requires scope: read:reports.

action.description: Read operation. Includes REST products/orders/customers/coupons, report totals, WooCommerce Analytics reports, and custom sales breakdowns.

label.description: WooCommerce connection label shown in AMCP integrations. Use woocommerce_list_stores first to discover labels.

payload.description: Action-specific body. Common pagination: { page?, perPage? }. LIST_PRODUCTS supports search/status/type/sku/category/tag/minPrice/maxPrice/onSale/inStock. LIST_ORDERS supports status/customer/product/after/before. GET_PRODUCT requires { productId }. GET_ORDER requires { orderId }. GET_SALES_REPORT / GET_TOP_SELLERS support { period? | dateMin/dateMax | startDate/endDate }. GET_REVENUE_STATS and *_STATS actions support { after|startDate, before|endDate, interval? }. GET_REPORT_TOTALS requires { report: "orders/totals" | "products/totals" | "customers/totals" | "coupons/totals" | "reviews/totals" | "categories/totals" | "tags/totals" | "attributes/totals" }. GET_ANALYTICS_REPORT requires { endpoint, expectList? } for any supported wc-analytics report endpoint. GET_SALES_BREAKDOWN supports { groupBy: date|product|sku|variation|category|coupon|status|country|customer|payment_method, interval: day|week|month|quarter|year, startDate/endDate, status?, maxPages?, perPage?, limit?, sortBy?, sortDir? }.

Supported syntax: * Filter expressions are made up of one or more restrictions. * Restrictions can be combined by the logical operator `AND`. * A restriction has the form of `{field} {operator} {value}`. * The `displayName` and `email` fields must use the `HAS (:)` operator. * The `lastLoginTime` field must use either the `LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO (<=)` or `GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO (>=)` operator. * All other fields must use the `EQUALS (=)` operator. Supported fields: * `assignedUserRole.advertiserId` * `assignedUserRole.entityType`: This is synthetic field of `AssignedUserRole` used for filtering. Identifies the type of entity to which the user role is assigned. Valid values are `Partner` and `Advertiser`. * `assignedUserRole.parentPartnerId`: This is a synthetic field of `AssignedUserRole` used for filtering. Identifies the parent partner of the entity to which the user role is assigned. * `assignedUserRole.partnerId` * `assignedUserRole.userRole` * `displayName` * `email` * `lastLoginTime` (input in ISO 8601 format, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) Examples: * The user with `displayName` containing "foo": `displayName:"foo"` * The user with `email` containing "bar": `email:"bar"` * All users with standard user roles: `assignedUserRole.userRole="STANDARD"` * All users with user roles for partner 123: `assignedUserRole.partnerId="123"` * All users with user roles for advertiser 123: `assignedUserRole.advertiserId="123"` * All users with partner level user roles: `entityType="PARTNER"` * All users with user roles for partner 123 and advertisers under partner 123: `parentPartnerId="123"` * All users that last logged in on or after 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z (format of ISO 8601): `lastLoginTime>="2023-01-01T00:00:00Z"` The length of this field should be no more than 500 characters. provenance.meaning: The tool names, input schemas, actions and routes of the captured catalog, frozen as the naming-compatibility denominator (owner decision D17), and the files they were generated from. capture.shipped lists the capture files this tree ships, each verified against its captured digest; capture.withheld counts the ones it does not ship, whose digests cannot be checked here.
provenance.normalization: Each input digest is the SHA-256 of the file text with CRLF line ends read as LF.
